critical_errors.issue: The proof incorrectly claims that the construction used in Gubler–Jell–Rabinoff Proposition 9.6 supplies an auxiliary tropicalization separating the entire compact support of an arbitrary (n-1,n-1) test form from the analytic boundary. That published proof separates a chosen full-dimensional Abhyankar point; the underlying CLD Proposition 3.4.4 applies to compact sets consisting of points y with d_K(y)=n. An arbitrary (n-1,n-1) form can have support at points with d_K(y)=n-1 (and for n=1 it is a (0,0) function whose support may contain rigid points), so the required hypothesis is not established. Consequently, the existence of a target form ω compactly supported in Ω=G(U)\G(∂U) and representing the chosen α is unjustified. Without it, div(ψ_i)=0 over Ω cannot be paired with arbitrary α, and the central conclusion d'd''[h_i]=0 does not follow.

repair_hints: [pi_ef4b8ab22822f1ccc0242d30] Replace the boundary-avoidance paragraph with a proved localization result applicable to arbitrary compactly supported (n-1,n-1) test forms, establishing after refinement by the chart tropicalizing each test form that its representative ω is compactly supported in G(U)\G(∂U). Alternatively, reorganize the argument face-by-face around the full-dimensional Abhyankar points supporting the tropical curvature and prove that this localization suffices to recover the pairing with every analytic test form. Only after that may the coefficient-separation argument be used to deduce d'd''[h_i]=0 and invoke CLD Theorem 18.8.4.
